AUTHOR: Knausgård
TITLE: Temperate fish detection and classification: a deep learning based approach
REGION: Southern and western Norway (Austevoll, Agder, Trøndelag; Skagerrak coast)
SPECIES: Classification: Symphodus melops (male/female), Pollachius pollachius, Pollachius virens; dataset also includes Ctenolabrus rupestris, Centrolabrus exoletus, Gadus morhua, Molva molva, Melanogrammus aeglefinus, Squalus acanthias
DATA: Own temperate dataset (GoPro HERO4-7 at 2-5 m reef sites; stereo-BRUV at 8-35 m), 619 detection images / 1022 classification images; Fish4Knowledge (27,230 images) for classifier pre-training
V_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'spanning depths from 1-40 meters ... This ensured that the dataset reflects the natural variability in visibility and light conditions'; no performance stratified by visibility
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'The dataset for this experiment was randomly split in a 70% for training and 30% for verification'; Sec. 4.2: 'divided into 70% training images, 15% validation images, and 15% testing images'
R_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'verification is part of a live stream from an underwater camera located near a semi-submerged restaurant ... highly variable lighting conditions, and different camera angles not part of our training data' (qualitative samples only, Fig. 8)
C_EV: no statement found (only mAP@50 / IoU reported; Sec. 4.1 notes 'a tiny percentage of false objects ... erroneously detected as fish' without a rate)
E_EV: Sec. 5: 'The object detection approaches a mean average precision of 86.96%, and the CNN-SENet architecture achieves the state-of-the-art accuracy of 99.27%' (detection/classification metrics only)
ARCH: YOLOv3 (Darknet-53) fish detector + CNN-SENet (5 conv layers with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks) species classifier; benchmarked vs Inception-V3, ResNet-50, Inception-ResNet-V2
METR: Detection: mAP@0.5 (86.96%), average IoU 0.68; classification: test accuracy (99.27% F4K; 83.68% / 87.74% temperate without/with augmentation), confusion matrices, 10-run box plots
NOTE: R1 = Y is debatable: the detector was tried on a live stream from a different camera/site (restaurant camera) with different lighting and angles, but only qualitative examples (Fig. 8, YouTube link) are shown - no metric, hence R3 = N and R_ALL = P; a stricter coder may set R1 = N. Pre-training: YOLOv3 on ImageNet, classifier on Fish4Knowledge (coded 수중 데이터셋). F4K classification split is random at image level despite F4K containing trajectories (same-video frames); paper notes this property but does not treat it as leakage. NIMG = 619 detection + 1022 temperate classification images (F4K 27,230 excluded). Platform mixed: unbaited GoPro at wrasse reef sites plus stereo-BRUV rigs. Counting per species is stated as a system capability (Sec. 2) but never evaluated. FPS: live 25 FPS stream.
